citeAs: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang (2024). Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv:2408.01091.
creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)
description: The Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) benchmark evaluates the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in recognizing conflicting commands. It comprises 20,000 conflicts, evenly distributed between language-language (L-L) and vision-language (V-L) paradigms, spanning 8 tasks including RuleConflict, AttributeConflict, ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, OCRConflict, FigureConflict, GeometricConflict, and SemanticConflict. It is constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate.
name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) benchmark - self-contradictory variant
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: LLM evaluation agents were validated against human expert evaluations. GPT-4 achieved a Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.881 and 94% concordance with human experts on GPT-4V replies; LLaVA-1.5 replies showed 0.999 Spearman correlation and 99% concordance; Gemini replies showed 0.854 Spearman correlation and 97% concordance.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts manually selected subsets SCI-Core (1% of SCI-All) and SCI-Base (10% of SCI-All) with extra effort to guarantee diversity for ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, and OCRConflict. Human experts also evaluated LMM replies on SCI-Core for V-L tasks to determine whether replies successfully identify the conflict.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed using AutoCreate, an automatic dataset creation framework that leverages programs and large language models. AutoCreate starts from manually input seeds and maintains a seed pool. During each cycle, it includes two branches (language and vision), each with a Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner. Human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking quality. For SemanticConflict, images are retrieved from the ImageNet dataset.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of LLM-generated text conflicts and programmatically generated images. For SemanticConflict, images are sourced from the ImageNet dataset (imagenet-1k validation set). Seeds are manually crafted task-relevant inputs that seed the AutoCreate generation pipeline.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms; more modalities will be included in future work. No fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. No detailed study is provided on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For FigureConflict, the data dictionary is tampered with by changing the largest value to the smallest value before plotting. For GeometricConflict, object descriptions are modified by exchanging two attributes to introduce confusion. For SemanticConflict, the correct class label in questions is substituted with a similar but different object. OCR images vary in font, size, and color to augment diversity.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A Cleaner component removes data that does not meet quality standards. Human experts rigorously checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. The resulting high-quality dataset is refined to extract new seeds for re-entry into the seed pool. For ForbbidenConflict, an LLM agent judges whether generated questions have unique answers.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The SCI benchmark provides a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies. The AutoCreate framework facilitates the creation of diverse instruction datasets, promoting inclusivity in AI research. By improving dissonance detection, the approach boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems, essential for societal integration.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect and recognize self-contradictory or conflicting instructions in both language-language and vision-language paradigms. The benchmark is intended to advance human-computer interaction and communication technologies, and to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs) are used throughout the AutoCreate pipeline for generating text conflicts, extracting attributes, generating questions, and quality checking. GPT-4 is used as an evaluation agent to assess LMM replies. LLM agents are used to judge uniqueness of generated questions in ForbbidenConflict generation.
